_comment: The export contract for the silver tables `gh agile export` writes.
A CSV carries no schema, so without this every consumer guesses: `number` as
text, a duration as a float, an empty `time_to_first_review` as 0 rather than
null. This file exists so a loader can generate correct DDL without inspecting
data, and `tests/test_export_catalog.py` fails when it drifts from what the
export actually produces.
Singer/Meltano catalog shape, because that is what the consumers already read.
NOT `agile_catalog.json`. That name is taken: it is ExperienceFlowAI's GOLD
catalog, lives outside this repository and describes the `agile_*` tables. What
is here is silver -- GitHub's facts under GitHub's names -- and the `github_`
prefix is the reminder. See GOLD_MODEL.md.
Conventions that apply throughout, and that a type alone cannot say:
Durations are an integer count of SECONDS and no column name carries a unit
suffix. In days, cycle times reported 0.0 and a median of 0.0 was published as
a measurement. A null duration means an endpoint is missing -- an unreviewed
pull request has no `time_to_first_review` -- and is NOT zero.
Timestamps are ISO8601 UTC with a trailing Z. Absent is null.
Lists are joined with a SEMICOLON and typed as strings, not arrays. Promising
an array would oblige a loader to split them, and then this file would own the
escaping rule for a separator appearing inside a value. `labels`, `assignees`,
`reviewers`, `sprint_starts`, `closes_issues`, `keys`, `repos`.
`exported_at` stamps every row of every stream with the run that produced it,
so a loader concatenating several exports keeps their order without deriving
it from a filename.
REPLICATION KEYS, stated rather than guessed. The three incremental streams are
filtered by ONE watermark applied to the ISSUE's `updated_at` -- and for
`github_prs` by the pull request's `updated_at`, server-side, via `updated:>=`.
An event's `occurred_at` is NOT what the incremental window was applied to: an
old event on a recently-touched issue is re-exported, and a new event on an
untouched issue is not. Declaring `occurred_at` as the replication key would
tell a consumer something untrue, so `github_events` declares none and is
resolved on `event_hash` instead. Incremental runs deliberately overlap and
re-send rows; every stream is idempotent on its key_properties.
PROGRESS OF A CONTAINER is `sub_issues_done` over `sub_issues_total`. Three things
about that pair cannot be said by a type, and each has produced a wrong number.
PER LEVEL, NOT TRANSITIVE. `subIssuesSummary` counts DIRECT children, so an
initiative's tally is epics closed and an epic's is stories closed. Measured:
closing one story took its epic to 1/1 while the initiative above it stayed
0/1. Summing these across levels, or reading an initiative's as a count of
stories, produces a figure nobody can reconcile with the board.
`done` MEANS CLOSED, NOT COMPLETED. GitHub's field is named `completed` and it
counts children closed as NOT_PLANNED as well -- measured on issue 9, six of
seven with one abandoned. A dashboard labelling this `completed` asserts
something false about that row. The board's own column legend says `closed` for
exactly this reason, and so should anything built on these two columns.
0/0 IS A LEAF, NOT UNKNOWN AND NOT ZERO PERCENT. Both columns are 0 for an
issue with no children, which is every story and every bug. A story is not a
container and has no progress of this kind; render it as absent rather than as
an empty bar. `type:` tells you which rows the pair is meaningful for.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. An issue labelled `type:task` is NOT exported, in any stream.
A task is story-internal housekeeping -- many teams keep the same thing in a
markdown checklist -- and it has no metric and no KPI attached to it. It carries
no story points, is never given a `sprint:` label, and is on no board, so a row
for one would change no number in any downstream model. A grain exists to be
measured; this one would not be. Its events are dropped with it, since an event
row referencing an issue with no `github_issues` row is a foreign key into
nothing. Stated here rather than left as an absence, because a contract silent
about an exclusion reads as an oversight. Decided on AGILE-137; reversible, and
the data is still in GitHub if it is ever wanted.

metadata.comment: Keyed on repository AND number: a board may span repositories and both have a #12.

_additionalProperties_comment: `field_<name>` columns are the project's own fields, lower-cased with spaces
as underscores, and a project may define any of them. The five `setup`
creates are declared below with their types; anything else a project adds
arrives as an extra column, which is why this schema is open.

issue_key.description: Jira-style, from the key: label or the profile, e.g. AGILE-93. Falls back to owner/repo#93 when no key applies.

number.description: Per repository, shared with pull requests, never reused.

state_reason.description: COMPLETED, NOT_PLANNED, REOPENED, or empty. Finished and abandoned are not the same thing.

labels.description: Semicolon-joined. Carries type:, key: and sprint:.

assignees.description: Semicolon-joined logins. Point-in-time: who has it now, not who did the work.

epic_number.description: The epic this issue belongs to, null when its parent is not an epic. Unjoinable on its own across repositories -- prefer epic_key.

epic_title.description: Empty when the parent is not an epic.

epic_key.description: The epic this issue belongs to, as a key: AGILE-9. Joins to issue_key in one column. Empty when the parent is not an epic.

parent_key.description: The parent issue at whatever level, as a key. GitHub numbers issues per repository, so a number alone is ambiguous on a board spanning them -- this is not.

parent_type.description: The parent's type: initiative above an epic, epic above a story. Empty when the issue has no parent.

initiative_slug.description: The initiative this issue belongs to, from its own initiative: label, which `initiative reconcile` maintains down the whole tree. Join to the github_issues row whose type is initiative and whose slug matches.

sub_issues_total.description: DIRECT children only, so an initiative counts epics and an epic counts stories. 0 for a leaf, which is not the same as unknown. Paired with `sub_issues_done`; see PROGRESS OF A CONTAINER above.

sub_issues_done.description: GitHub's name is `completed`; it counts CLOSED children whatever reason they closed for, NOT_PLANNED included -- so this is `closed`, not `completed`. DIRECT children only. See PROGRESS OF A CONTAINER above.

reported_by.description: Who opened it. GitHub's author cannot be changed afterwards, so it is a stronger reporter than Jira's.

sprint_starts.description: Semicolon-joined YYYY-MM-DD, oldest first: every sprint the issue was worked in. From the sprint: labels, which survive an iteration write; field_sprint does not.

started_at.description: First arrival at In Progress, from the issue timeline. Not derivable from project item state.

cycle_time.description: SECONDS from started_at to done_at. Null when either end is missing.

worked_by.description: The closing pull request's author, else whoever moved it to review or done.

field_status.description: Project single-select: Todo, In Progress, Blocked, In Review, Done.

field_sprint.description: The iteration's title as the project holds it NOW. Cleared board-wide by any iteration write -- believe sprint_starts where they disagree.

field_story_points.description: Number, not integer: half points are a real convention.

field_title.description: GitHub's built-in Title field on the project item.

field_start_date.description: The epic's planned start, a project DATE field. A PLAN, not a measurement: `board show`'s roadmap derives when work actually began from the `sprint:` labels beneath an item, and the two are not interchangeable. Null on anything nobody dated, which is most rows.

field_target_date.description: The epic's planned finish, a project DATE field. The baseline a slip is measured against; null on anything nobody dated. See `field_start_date`.

metadata.comment: No replication-key, deliberately. The watermark filters the ISSUE on updated_at, so occurred_at is not the field the window was applied to. Resolve latest-wins on event_hash.

event_hash.description: sha256 over issue|kind|occurred|actor|previousStatus|status|detail, or over the pull request's node ids. Stable across exports so an overlapping run overwrites rather than duplicates. Timestamps are per-second and two changes in one second are ordinary, which is why it is not issue|kind|occurred alone.

process_type.description: Which object the row is about. change-request-opened appears under BOTH: once scoped to the issue a pull request closes, once to the pull request itself.

issue_key.description: Empty for a pull request closing no issue.

event_name.description: Named for the action, not GitHub's object, so a transform maps it without knowing what a pull request is.

actor_name.description: Who did it. On a review this is the REVIEWER, which no issue event distinguishes.

state.description: The status moved to, or a review's APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED / COMMENTED / DISMISSED.

was_automated.description: Status changes only; null on every other event.

metadata.comment: The only stream GitHub filters for us: `updated:>=<watermark>` in the search query, so an incremental run never transfers a pull request nobody touched.

schema._content_comment: No diff hunk, no patch, no review or comment body. These rows make events and metrics, not code analysis.

changes_requested_total.description: Review round-trips: how often it came back.

time_to_first_review.description: SECONDS, created to first review. Null when never reviewed -- NOT zero.

time_to_merge.description: SECONDS, created to merged. Null when not merged.

metadata.comment: Master data: small, changes rarely, reloaded whole. A watermark over it would be a way to miss the one change that mattered.

repos.description: Semicolon-joined. A board may span repositories.

sprint_cadence.description: The profile's hand-authored cadence_days -- a person writes 14. The one place a day count survives, and the suffix stops at the file's edge.

board_id.description: The view number, as `board list` prints it.

filter.description: The view's own filter, verbatim. Empty means the board excludes nothing.

metadata.comment: Iterations carry no stable id: any configuration write re-mints every one of them, so a sprint is identified by name and date here rather than by id.

duration.description: DAYS, and the exception that proves the rule: it is GitHub's own field on the iteration, reproduced verbatim rather than converted.
